column1: # Seamly measurement names and the Toile catalogue names they stand for.
# The owner decided, for the mannequin plan, that the names Seamly gives its
# measurements live in a data file of their own and nowhere in the code, so an
# audit of the licence of the source tree meets none of them. This is that
# file: the importer reads it and nothing else to rename a body's measurements.
# Format: one mapping per line, the Seamly name, a tab, the Toile name. Lines
# starting with '#' and blank lines are ignored. Each Toile name must be one of
# MeasureSet::CATALOGUE, and each side may appear on one line only; a test
# holds the file to both.
# Provenance: every Seamly name here was read in the owner's own measurement
# file, never in Seamly's sources. A row is added only where both names mean
# the same measurement taken the same way, which is why most of the owner's
# measurements have none. Those stay out of the imported body and are listed
# in the import report.
#   height            stature, standing, to the floor (Toile: the body's height)
#   waist_circ        girth at the waist
#   hip_circ          girth at the hip
#   leg_crotch_to_floor
#                     down the inside of the leg from the fork to the floor,
#                     which is what Toile's inseam measures
#   neck_mid_circ     neck girth at mid-neck, where Toile cuts its neck ring
#   bust_circ         girth at the bust
#   shoulder_tip_to_shoulder_tip_b
#                     across the back from one shoulder point to the other
height
waist_circ
hip_circ
leg_crotch_to_floor
neck_mid_circ
bust_circ
shoulder_tip_to_shoulder_tip_b
